source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The cited article studies BATEC identification, uniform estimation and bands for distance-based methods; its score density is continuous and bounded away from zero, and Theorem 6 is a distance-based minimax lower bound.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:math/0410354v3, corresponding to Mathematical Methods of Statistics 14 (2005)
source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 3–4, Theorems 1–2 and the exp(-1/h^alpha) example
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper treats one-dimensional pointwise regression under regularly and Gamma-varying degenerate design and obtains logarithmically slow severe-degeneracy rates.
The paper constructs a local-polynomial estimator with a Lepski-type selector, adaptive at one query point to unknown local design scarcity and local smoothness.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:math/0509634, corresponding to Statistics & Probability Letters 77 (2007), 782–794
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper gives an unknown-density spatially normalized sup-norm estimator and an inhomogeneous confidence band under a positive continuous univariate design density.
The paper gives spatially varying uniform rates for univariate random-design regression with finitely many polynomial density zeros and an adaptive estimator.
The paper considers known univariate designs with finitely many well-separated polynomial or exponential zeros, global L2 minimax lower bounds, and adaptive wavelet estimators.

source_verification_receipts.version: Annals of Statistics 42 (2014), 1787–1818 electronic reprint; arXiv:1303.7152v4
source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 1–2, abstract; p. 6, Theorem 2.1; p. 10, Theorem 3.1
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper proves Gaussian anti-concentration and a generic honest-band result that accommodates data-selected resolutions under its stated studentization and coupling conditions.
The paper develops bias-aware honest scalar intervals for nonparametric regression, together with efficiency comparisons and optimal bandwidth calculations.
The paper gives pointwise k-NN adaptation using local ball-mass growth and locally selected neighborhood sizes.
